author: Sean Graney
title: Jackson Chamber hosts first-ever Community Impact Day - NewsBreak
text:
By Sean Graney ,
3 hours ago
JACKSON, Mich. (WLNS) — Community members across Jackson rolled up their sleeves on Wednesday for a day dedicated to service and giving back.
The first ever Jackson Community Impact Day paired businesses and residents with projects benefiting nonprofits and local neighborhoods. Jacob Inosencio with Grow Jackson says this initiative is about giving Michiganders new ways to get involved and give back.
Volunteers painting at the Jackson County Fairgrounds. (WLNS) “Whether it’s a big community impact volunteer event or it’s building a food hub or it’s hosting the farmers market here, we’re just really excited to say, ‘How can we participate? How can we help develop our community?'” Inosencio said.
Chamber leaders say Jackson joined a growing statewide movement focused on service, collaboration, and community impact.
“Today is actually one of the largest mobilizations of volunteers throughout the year in our state,” Buchanan said. “So we joined in that opportunity and we’re excited…we’ve got over 100 volunteers today at about 15 locations.”
Volunteers Shoveling Dirt at the River and Rail Food Hub. (Alex Scott) Buchanan says many of the projects tackled at the event may seem small at first, but she says they can make a major impact in the long run.
“Some of these projects don’t seem like such a large project, but to a nonprofit organization, it means the world,” Buchanan said. “They don’t necessarily have the time to work on these projects on their own.”
Volunteers working at Disability Connections in Jackson. (WLNS) Inosencio says events like this can bring people together regardless of background or differences.
“I don’t know what you think about this or that, the other thing, but I know that we care about food,” Inosencio said. “I know we care about the community, and we can build a relationship around that.”
